newsitem.title: USA: Theragenics, Johnson & Johnson sign pact.
newsitem.headline: Theragenics, Johnson & Johnson sign pact.

text.p: Medical equipment manufacturer Theragenics Corp said Tuesday it had signed a letter of intent granting Johnson & Johnson the right to sell a Theragenics device for the treatment of prostate cancer.
Theragenics said the letter grants J&J unit Indigo Medical Inc the exclusive worldwide right to market and sell TheraSeed, a Palladium 103 product.
The initial term of the agreement is seven years, with automatic extensions of three years each as long as certain performance criteria are met, Theragenics said.
The company said it expects to finalize the arrangements during the second quarter.
Also, J&J's J&J Development Corp will invest $5.0 million in Theragenics common stock, Theragenics said.
On Monday Theragenics shares closed at 18-1/8 on the Nasdaq National Market.
Theragenics is based in Norcross, Ga.
